notes: Ten SFist items were queued and three had text worth reading for an address; the Bayshore Freeway repaving story names no street number, and the two roundup columns were read in full for the items that do. Both findings here are from stories about what happened to a building rather than about who was in it, and no person named in either story is recorded. The chocolatier in the Dogpatch story is the proprietor of the business, not an architect, builder or developer, so only the business is named.

coverage.note: Two numbered addresses appeared across the three stories read, and both produced a finding. The freeway repaving story and the two SFUSD/California Forever items on other feeds are outside this file.

findings.description: SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts launched a public art partnership, Yerba Buena Illuminated, whose first work is a 95-foot piece by Los Angeles artist Jennifer Steinkamp, "It's a nice day for a white wedding", projected onto the facade of the Humboldt Bank Building. The building is the work's surface, not its venue: the partnership is described as continuing, so the parcel is named as the site of the series rather than of a single evening's event.

findings.description: The Shekoh Culinary Institute is opening in September 2026 in a second-floor studio in this Dogpatch building, running in-person cooking and chocolate workshops from 9 September alongside online classes. The same second-floor kitchen has held the proprietor's online chocolate business for about a year. The story is dated to publication rather than to the first class, because the opening is stated as a month and the 9 September date is the first session rather than the institute's opening.

citation.label: SFist, “Local Chocolatier to Open Culinary Institute In SF’s Dogpatch,” 25 August 2026
